# gluetun post-rules for m1.home — applied inside the VPN client after the tunnel is up.
# Generated by kiwi-server; the fleet file is the place to change it.
# MTU: no TCP segment bigger than the tunnel carries — its MTU less 40 bytes of IPv4
# and TCP headers, on every SYN both ways. Not --clamp-mss-to-pmtu: it reads only the
# interface a SYN leaves by, and the way back can be narrower. --set-mss never raises
# a smaller MSS.
iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp -m tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1336
# forwarding (gluetun's policy is DROP): no hairpin on eth0; replies to what went out;
# what the DNAT rules below redirect; the docker network out through the tunnel.
iptables -A FORWARD -i eth0 -o eth0 -j REJECT
iptables -A FORWARD -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
iptables -A FORWARD -i tun0 -m conntrack --ctstate DNAT -j ACCEPT
iptables -A FORWARD -s 172.128.0.0/24 -o tun0 -j ACCEPT
# LAN clients the gateway module routes through this container
iptables -A FORWARD -i eth0 -o tun0 -j ACCEPT
# mesh access: traffic for this node's mesh address on 80/443 goes to the reverse proxy
iptables -t nat -A PREROUTING -d 10.8.0.6 -p tcp --dport 443 -j DNAT --to-destination 172.128.0.5:443
iptables -t nat -A PREROUTING -d 10.8.0.6 -p tcp --dport 80 -j DNAT --to-destination 172.128.0.5:80
# mesh SSH: port 22 of the mesh address to the machine's sshd (the docker gateway is the host)
iptables -t nat -A PREROUTING -d 10.8.0.6 -p tcp --dport 22 -j DNAT --to-destination 172.128.0.1:22
iptables -t nat -A PREROUTING -d 10.8.0.6 -p tcp --dport 2224 -j DNAT --to-destination 172.128.0.251:22
# NAT: everything leaving through the tunnel
iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -o tun0 -j MASQUERADE
# replies to what we sent out
iptables -A INPUT -i tun0 -m state --state RELATED,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
